question: Does holding facility types, technologies and build types as numbers, after zones, nations, unit types and marks, and reading Improved Factories without a full catalog context, leave play unchanged, and what does it save?
machine: Apple M4 Max: 10 performance and 4 efficiency cores, 36 GB

searched_games.network: 64x2 networks with random-filled first-layer tables (tools/replay_coordinator_rounds.py --make-weights), evaluated one position at a time

cpu_seconds_first_pair.caveat: A profiling run (one more game process) overlapped most of this pair's first run of this change and the first half-minute of its marks run; the bracketed pair above was run again, with nothing else of this study running, for that reason.

profiles.how: /usr/bin/sample for 60 s of one searched game (seed 41), from 25 s after it started, one process; shares of the engine's samples (those under the Python binding), each counting a sample once if the function is on its stack
profiles.overhead: Engine samples whose innermost function compares strings, allocates or frees, copies memory or looks up a map
profiles.caveat: Each profile covers 60 s of the same game; the faster build gets further in that time, so the positions sampled differ a little.

notes: The bracketed searched games ran in the order: this change, the marks build, this change, back to back on the same Mac, with nothing else of this study running.

Instruction counts of repeated searched-game runs of one build differ by about 1% (marks build 5,557 and 5,601 G; this change 5,334, 5,386 and 5,321 G); CPU seconds depend more on the Mac's other work.
